The Prophet gave pre-emption in every joint undivided property, but none once the boundaries are marked and the ways and streets fixed.
The Prophet ruled pre-emption (Shuf'a) for every undivided joint property, but none once the limits are marked and the ways and streets fixed.
Short of food, Abu Ubaida's army and the Ash'aris pooled their provisions and shared them equally, the Prophet blessed a pooled heap, and a camel's meat was split ten ways.
The right of pre-emption holds in every jointly owned property until the land is divided and its ways are marked out.
The Prophet blessed the young Abdullah bin Hisham instead of taking his pledge, and later Ibn Umar and Ibn Az-Zubair sought him as their partner in buying foodstuff.
